correctness.rationale: The h^1 Poisson-measure norm identity is proved using weak-* compactness and positivity of the Poisson approximate identity. Equality at each signed Fourier frequency forces a unit phase character, with the gcd ideal determining exactly one cyclic support coset; the converse is immediate. Quantitative stability follows from the exact 2(1-|hat mu|) L2 phase identity, a finite integer Bezout telescoping certificate, circle sine geometry and a nearest-coset pushforward. Two nearby atoms prove the square-root exponent sharp. The actual packaged standard-library checker passed 135 exact-support, 180 quantitative and 15 sharpness test cases; no finite calculation is treated as a general proof.

value.rationale: The natural question of all equality cases at the recently determined sharp h1 constant has a nontrivial arithmetic answer across every finite set S. Maximal Poisson pole number equals a gcd that varies with frequency spacing, sharply contrasting 1<p<infinity rigidity. The theorem also gives explicit bounded-Lipschitz near-extremizer control from measured coefficient deficits, with the optimal square-root exponent proved by a two-point family. It is a structural complete family classification and robust boundary, not a substitute or routine rephrasing of the single Poisson example.
